reviews.text: Daisy and Sebastian were able to shine in their depictions of strangers-to-lovers – delivering chilling scenes through their intoxicating relationship and bringing a sense of vulnerability and poise to their roles, respectively.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: “Fresh” is a stylish, uncompromising, and surprisingly artistic depiction of endemic exploitation, the ubiquity of toxic masculinity, and perseverance.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: Watch it for the great performances, but don’t expect to be blown away.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: A raw, nasty, horrifying, but electrifying. A spiraling thriller that continues to twist all the way up to the end. Daisy Jones is INCREDIBLE & Sebastian Stan turns in his best performance yet.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Mimi Cave delivers an extraordinarily captivating, assertive directorial debut; taking Lauryn Kahn's original, gruesome screenplay to the next level (...) holding all of the characteristics to become a cult classic.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The writing is never offensively straightforward either, yet there are times the script veers toward middle-of-the-road in the face of such an unusual premise and outcome.
reviews.author: Paul Lê

reviews.text: Fresh is an outlandish comedy-thriller that exposes the exaggerated horrors of dating in the digital age. It balances its dark, satirical humor with a lighthearted romance angle and carries unsettling and unpredictable turns throughout.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Mimi Cave’s Hulu horror movie Fresh gives us a new version of the All-American Monster.
reviews.author: Jenn Adams

reviews.text: Fresh is about the horrors of dating as a young woman...that itching feeling that something could go wrong, the urge to text someone the address, and the imaginary escape route planned while feigning a smile.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: Fresh may be a little messy at times but it does not detract from this delectable debut from Cave and a solid screenplay from Kahn.
reviews.author: Cidnya Silva

reviews.text: "While the execution leaves room for minor improvements, Fresh is a highly commendable debut."
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: The ultimate meat-cute... Fresh is wild, wicked and deliciously entertaining. Just don’t see it on a first date, or else there likely won’t be a second.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Deliciously sinister and delectably unhinged. Sebastian Stan has never been more sizzlingly hot and Daisy Edgar-Jones gives a raw, unguarded, and toothsome performance.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: Undercooked, overseasoned.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Fresh offers the kinds of laughs that make you break off in the middle as you realize where the humor resides. You'll either love it or hate it.
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: Edgar-Jones’s Noa taps hidden reserves of pluck as she fights for her survival against her deranged captor. She’s a horror heroine you root for all the way to the bloody end.
reviews.author: Taylor Antrim

reviews.text: Daisy Edgar-Jones and Sebastian Stan star in this dark comedy-horror that’s subtextually about toxic relationships and the commodification of women, but on the surface is about a relationship with a quirky cannibal gone wrong.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: It’s an enjoyable movie, with a firm grasp on genre history, some effectively shocking visuals (the freezer, ugh), and a solid cast.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text:
An absolute triumph.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: If you want to see a pretty good rom-com starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Sebastian Stan turn into a pretty great satirical horror movie about the commodification of the self through social media and dating apps, point your browser to Disney+ and hit play.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: A film that keeps getting called in various directions until none of them offer up any palpable suspense, fun or satire.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Fresh is a reminder that putting yourself out there in any form, especially if that entails trusting a stranger, can bite you in the ass. literally.
reviews.author: Lina Lecaro

reviews.text: One can only imagine it would be hard to imagine yourself in this situation in real life but Jones is brilliant at putting the audience in Noa shoes (or chair...wink wink)
reviews.author: Stephanie Chapman

reviews.text: Fresh manages the trick of being gross but engaging.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: The savory gimmick is delivered flawlessly. Fresh gets under the skin without limiting itself to the usual gross-out approaches we've consistently seen. Stan offers irresistible charm as well.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: The worst date turned into a delightfully gory horror film.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: Fresh keeps going farther than we might expect it to, yet keeping a firm hold on its quasi-comic tone.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Fresh becomes too focused on upsetting you as the film goes on, but as Get Out showed so masterfully, some insightful messages can be hidden within a fantastical storyline. A must-watch for horror fans, provided they have eaten first.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Go into this film as blind as possible and prepare to be shocked and thoroughly entertained.
reviews.author: Mike Muncer

reviews.text: A dark horror comedy about the dangers and struggles of modern dating with a fresh take on the execution.
reviews.author: Amanda the Jedi

reviews.text: While the film does linger at times, underutilizing a few characters along the way, Fresh is a welcomed addition to the world of horror.
reviews.author: Stephanie Archer

reviews.text: ...processed, snackable but not nourishing
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: By the time 'Fresh' reaches its conclusion, you want Noa to best him in this sick cat-and-mouse game. Steve joins a character archetype of horror psychopaths that will make people think twice about the advances of a stranger with quick wit and a smile.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Fresh strikes a fine balance between blood and gore, story and message, and unsettling scenes offset by macabre humor.
reviews.author: Brian Costello

reviews.text: The film’s easy to stay with – though there’s some genuinely queasy takes that may have you rethinking your dinner plans – and I really admired how and where they splashed in the title credits.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Deliciously demented, if a bit long, Fresh is best served to a blind audience who don't know the surprises it has in store for them.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: A really good movie you can recommend to almost no one.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the cruder the story grows, the less stimulating it becomes, no matter how efficiently crafted some scenes may look.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Despite its original style and great performances, Fresh doesn't go beyond its interesting and disturbing premise about the horrors of modern dating.
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: An effective horror thriller: it’s pacey, well visualised and not too predictable.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: Fresh is a dark and funny film that takes our modern dating fears into the realm of extremity, a movie unafraid to sharpen its knives and slice up standard cinematic tropes in an effort to make something new and different. Dont be afraid to dig in.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: This anti-rom-com serves its thrills raw and decidedly bloody.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Mimi Cave's directorial debut takes a scalpel to what could have been a rather dour and conventional, exploitative tale and peppers it with strangely romantic & twisted black comic gusto.
reviews.author: Tony Black

reviews.text: You’ll eat it up.  And be sure to pair it with a nice chianti.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Comically twisting the source genre away from the concept of the Final Girl, Fresh celebrates female camaraderie, resourcefulness, and good humour in the face of monstrous behaviour.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: It’s as subtle as a sledgehammer, but Fresh’s audacious storytelling, full-throated performances and accomplished direction make for a tasty, wildly entertaining concoction.
reviews.author: Sophie Butcher

reviews.text: One moment, youre laughing in spite of yourself and the next youre sitting there uncomfortably because of the uncanny way the film utilizes familiar conversational topics surrounding dating and romance and mixes it with dark satire and horror.
reviews.author: Terry Mesnard

reviews.text: As a statement of intent from two emerging filmmakers -- this is Kahn’s second feature script -- Fresh makes a potent impression. It’s stylish and smart where it counts, even if it occasionally veers into the unnecessarily didactic.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: To frame it in Fresh’s own language, all we get here is a single bite -- not the whole steak.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Directed with verve and snappily written by Lauryn Kahn, this is an exciting feature debut for Cave. Equal parts hilarious and horrifying, Fresh should put viewers off both men and meatball dinners for at least  a few days.
reviews.author: Joel Harley

reviews.text: It takes you by surprise with its witty observations and staggering reveal; at the same time, it falls prey to shallow tropes of flimsy feminism and rote plotting.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: The whirr of subplots also resembles an over-extended tasting menu. Too many dishes fly by; the evening starts to feel like a long night.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: This movie will not be to everyone’s taste. But it is well made, well acted, and has clever, surprising twists towards the end. It marks the debut director as a filmmaker to watch.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: A twisted genre-flipper giving Sebastian Stan and Daisy Edgar-Jones meaty material to sink their teeth into.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: One of the best parts about a thriller is its ability to build a world and commit to its premise, and Fresh does both very well.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: A fantastic first act loses some energy as the film overstays its welcome with a draggy climax, but credit Sebastian Stan for his go-for-broke performance and Daisy Edgar-Jones for anchoring the whole enterprise. This one is plenty of fun
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: It’s a movie that deserves to spark conversation for quite some time. The dance scenes, the charisma, it’s all meant to seduce but, hopefully, to get us to think about an unavoidably complex subject.
reviews.author: Kimberly Ricci

reviews.text: Steves business is extreme. But that first act is important context: the film places Steves sadism on a continuum with other men Noa encounters in the dating world.
reviews.author: Orla Smith

reviews.text: Both its face value middle fingers and underlying moral deconstructions are tough sells made endlessly provocative.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Every aspect of Fresh feels well-tuned to the narrative's deeper thematic connotations.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: I really dug this. It is twisted, ambitious, and cool.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It certainly captures some of the horrors of the dating scene for modern women. Not for squeamish audiences.
reviews.author: Dana Han-Klein

reviews.text: It's one of those movies that relies on catching the viewer unaware, thus a trailer or review - even a poster - could give too much away and lessen your experience.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Writer Lauryn Kahn and director Mimi Cave have constructed a playful and captivating horror story bolstered by solid performances that does, at times, feel pretty fresh.
reviews.author: Kayla Kumari Upadhyaya

reviews.text: If you want to be terrified of meeting someone to date in real life as well as being terrified of online dating, Fresh is definitely the movie for you.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: An uncompromising, swing-for-the-fences directorial debut that greatly benefits from a committed performance from its wickedly charming leading man.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: "If you relish dark, devious psycho-thrillers, 'Fresh' may whet your appetite."
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Im quite the Peter Cetera fan, and Restless Heart will never sound the same to me ever again.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Mimi Cave brings us a stylish and bloody film that isnt without its inconsistencies. That being said, there are numerous effective and uncomfortable moments that will have viewers on edge. Edgar-Jones and Stan are electric together.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Theres a restraint on Cave's part to not go overboard or make it this in your face grotesque approach that you could have found under a different filmmaker looking for shock value.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: What comes next is a series of messed up twists that catapult the film out of rom-com territory and into the comedy-thriller zone...
reviews.author: Kate Robertson

reviews.text: Food porn gets a sick twist when a hot date goes off in a horror show with a fiendish sense of fun.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: ...a delectable and savory little treat.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: About 30 minutes into the film, the opening credits finally roll, and we’re off, taking a morbidly comedic turn towards the truly unsettling.
reviews.author: Adam Mullins-Khatib

reviews.text: The overall impression is one diminishing returns, the films few inspired instances and throwback horror sensibilities subsumed within a mess of filler. Fresh certainly isnt rotten, but it doesnt rise much above last nights leftovers either.
reviews.author: Luke Gorham

reviews.text: Call it Fifty Shades of Grey with Tabasco sauce.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Fresh delivers the whole package. Its a deliciously, twisted horror/comedy that leaves you craving more.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: A lightweight fun dating satire for people who love the grisly stuff.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Is Sebastian Stan the dullest actor working today?
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The most surprising thing about Fresh is that, given the audacity of the concept, the filmmakers pull it off.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: With a sharply energetic script from comedy screenwriter Lauryn Kahn, “Fresh” willfully borrows from both comedy and horror in a way that destabilizes the use of each.
reviews.author: Sarah-Tai Black

reviews.text: Like a lot of movies these days, Fresh feels like it was conceived through its themes first and then written to bolster those ideas, rather than from the perspective of character or story.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Ordering a thigh or breast takes on sinister new meaning in this deliciously twisted horror comedy that serves up some carnivorous sexual politics with a side of bloody revenge.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The irresistibility of Fresh lies in the fact that it doesnt take itself too seriously -- all things considered, the film manages to stay light on its feet with its Hostel meets Ex Machina concept.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: It’s by no means perfect – and the central premise may not be palatable to many people – but Fresh certainly lives up to its name, when it comes to horror-fuelled thrills.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Splatter movie, satire and slapstick come together and at last you can laugh. How sweet it is.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Cave’s cunning fizzles and fades a little in the third act, giving way to mostly rote violence and contrivances that’ll have you shouting advice at the screen. But as the opening volley from a filmmaker with wily vision, Fresh is aptly self-descriptive.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It's smart, dark & devious. If you have an appetite for fresh, original tales of dating disasters, this is bloody fun. It's not every day you get to feast on a uniquely twisted horror that doubles as a warning of the nightmares of today's dating game.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: There are many moments in Fresh that are hard to stomach, but those who arent turned off by such scenes will find a lot to enjoy.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Fresh emerges as a routine shockeroo trying desperately to be a meaningful, up-to-date reflection of the scary times we live in. Or at least to gross us out. Neither of which takes place.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Cave takes a light touch with the gore in this film, but she uses it to pointed affect. Unfortunately, Fresh ditches that ambiguity in favor of an otherwise straightforward survival plot that suffers in its inability to examine its characters too closely.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: A deliberately queasy mixture of cautionary tale, black comedy, cat-and-mouse intrigue, and grisly thriller, Fresh struck me as anything but...
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Takes a dramatic pivot into a completely different type of feminist sendup, one thats much less interesting or insightful.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Fresh is not for the squeamish and it earns every morsel of its R-rating. But if you can endure its disturbing macabre elements, you'll find a sickly satisfying chiller with more on its mind that you might think.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: This is a modern day feminism tale of women being manipulated by men, harvested for their bodies, and forced to fight their way out.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Its a likable debut from a filmmaker Im excited to see develop.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: It starts out as a deft examination of the angst of dating in the age of swiping left and right, and all too soon turns into a film that loses our sympathies as it turns nauseating.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: It has all the elements of a bloody thriller while also being humorous enough that it isnt a total decent into nihilism.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Mimi Cave brings forward a very peculiar style through a film that shines because of its performances, especially that of Sebastian Stan. This will obviously be big for fans of "Promising Young Woman," serial killer podcasts, and true crime stories.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: Wow.  Give me seconds!  I mean, a sequel.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: As the opening title card belatedly drops at the 30-minute mark, Cave's film announces that everything up until this point was prologue  and unfortunately, the blackly comic thriller it subsequently becomes is devoid of anything in the way of surprises.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: With plenty of visual style and two superb lead performances, Fresh is a surprising and twisted treat of a thriller that you won't want to miss.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Fresh is a cinematic meal thats best enjoyed exactly like the title says.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: The movie comes across as a mishmash of tones, approaches, and purposes.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: A top-tier horror movie from start to finish. Your chills will get chills.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Fresh wants to do  and say  everything.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: "Fresh" is a reminder to everyone fed up with the horrors of modern dating that things could be much, much worse.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: A balm to any singleton that promises to turn you off online dating and red meat forever.
reviews.author: Chandler Levack

reviews.text: If you saw Netflix's recent The Tinder Swindler and thought it was unsettling, then just wait until you get a load of Fresh.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Cave and screenwriter Lauryn Kahn apparently believe that theyre on the cutting edge here but this sort of very dark comedy is no longer the rarity it once was, and compared to some other recent examples...its neither terribly clever nor shocking.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Fresh is easily the most disturbing and twisted film I've seen in a long time.  Fresh had me laughing out loud.  Then gasping in abject disgust.  The film's subject matter is beyond macabre.  Don't watch Fresh on a full stomach.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Its a Midnight Movie unafraid to take its deadly dating metaphor to bloody extremes. It breathes the same air as movies like Promising Young Woman in its mix of modern allegory and horror, but when the going gets gruesome, it stands on its own.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Fresh doesn’t push the body horror as far as it could, and works better as an empowerment fable than as an actual thriller. But maybe that’s for the best.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: The movie isn't sunk by its sluggishness, with morbid interests always managing to keep the endeavor upright, contributing some decent nightmare fuel with real-world paranoia and fantasy appetites.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Despite its lack of subtleties or even the absence of character substance, not to mention a wildly over-the-top climax, its a wild ride
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The horror film Fresh is effectively terrifying and nauseating when the movie's gruesome surprise is revealed. What will disturb many viewers the most is that it's not just a contrived plot twist for a movie but something that could happen in real life.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Altogether this is a superb first-time feature: smart, provocative, unexpectedly weird and often very, very funny.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: the subject is taboo enough that filmmakers usually go one of two ways...But Fresh, while very well crafted, tries to play it in the middle somewhere with gore that isnt campy but disturbingly realistic, making for a truly unpleasant experience.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Ideas and flashy performances aren't enough to handwave away the many glaring problems here. The message the story does want to get across is not past its expiration date; its just rottenly told
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: “Fresh” is feminist horror with a rattlesnake bite to it. But you’ll need a strong stomach to watch it.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Cave creates an atmosphere in which — if you can stomach it — viewers will swallow just about anything that happens.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: A pitch-black metoo comedy thriller thats sick, depraved & perverted  but in a fun way.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Quirky editing and a few novel 1980s song choices aside, there's sadly not much about Fresh that's actually, well, fresh.
reviews.author: Jayne Nelson

reviews.text: Guilty pleasures rarely come more deviant than Mimi Cave’s Fresh, which takes Sebastian Stan and makes him bury Bucky Barnes forever.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: I am impressed at how Mimi Cave blended the genres and tones to create a thrilling and fun experience.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: Full of earned twists and turns, Fresh may be one of the best narrative features at Sundance this year. Moreover, its a film that ultimately creates intrigue and curiosity at the future works of Cave, Kahn, Edgar-Jones, and Stan.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Fresh is an exquisite horror delicacy...a good balance of flavors that hits the palate just right.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: An eye for detail on the eccentricities of modern dating leaves FRESH with an interesting but tonally weird film that finds itself struggling to maintain its energy without sacrificing its impact.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: Its darkness is not for everyone, but for some it works.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: While FRESH aims for progressiveness in its setups, it also falls into one typical trap after the next.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: Fresh has an engaging initial idea and a clever first act but it struggles to make good on the premise and its exploration of the commodification of women's bodies feels more interesting for what it might suggest than for anything the film does.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: FRESH... is about the horrors of online dating and features the most shocking turn by an Avenger (Sebastian Stan) since Chris Evans donned a wool sweater in Knives Out.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It’s very ambitious and well-executed for a first-time feature film, with impressive set designs and cinematography.
reviews.author: Carolyn Hinds

reviews.text: A provocative and twisted film that lets Sebastian Stan go off the rails.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: Fresh made me miss a meal or three. Mimi Cave's romantic horror satire (!) is a twisted lovechild of Promising Young Woman and Get Out - except it carves the modern dating and gender allegories into our hearts with a bloody steak knife.
reviews.author: Rahul Desai

reviews.text: Fresh isn't the first schlock-thriller about the horrors of dating, but few manage such a delicate balance of silly and smart.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: A sharp critique of the horrors of modern dating and a clever allegory for the exploitation of women's bodies, 'Fresh' is a deliciously nasty treat.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Writing about Fresh without giving away its secrets is pretty much impossible, so let's leave it at this: See it. Have fun. And maybe don't eat first.
reviews.author: Allison Shoemaker

reviews.text: It leaves a potent aftertaste, especially in its subtlety with regards to the reaction by others when women become victims to men's abuses. The true horror is the blame and pointed fingers that still seem to be pointed in the wrong direction.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: Mimi Cave's thriller, Fresh is smart, transgressive, stomach-churning fun that also offers a few sly insights into the modern dating game.
reviews.author: J.R. Kinnard

reviews.text: This is a searing example of sharp and intelligent filmmaking at its very best, and just happens to be intensely entertainment as well.
reviews.author: Wilson Kwong

reviews.text: A wild slice of horror from director Mimi Cave that features a go-for-broke performance by Sebastian Stan.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Fresh works best when it marries the grossness factor with slick black humor, percolating to a place of truly provocative horror.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: Perhaps this might be the moment that some start to pay attention to just how interesting and strange Stan's career outside of Marvel is because lord knows I'd love to see him in more stuff like this.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: FRESH is an impressive debut from filmmaker Mimi Cave and serves as a takedown and a warning about the dangers of modern dating.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: Sebastian Stan is wicked sexy in this horror, thriller that makes a gruesome stance on modern day dating. It's like Silence of thee Lambs meets Black Dahlia in the best way possible
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Once limbs start to fly and blood is splattered by the gallon, Fresh reveals itself to be just another horror film, one that would be labeled as misogynist were it made by a male director.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The final act comes with perhaps too many surprises on the menu, but the film is so much fun that I didn't mind the extra courses.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: Fresh is a commentary on modern dating that's meant to be an exaggeration, yet feels too familiar in many ways, making the ending all the more cathartic.
reviews.author: Alysha Prasad

reviews.text: Led by those two strong performances, a very tight script by Kahn, and Cave's dynamic direction, Fresh is horror done right. It's got a message, it executes it with precision, and it will freak you out on a number of levels.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: Fresh is not for the squeamish, but it is one hell of horror smorgasbord. In addition, it provides a fascinating metaphor for the meat market that women are forced to deal with when it comes to modern dating.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: It may not work as social commentary horror, but Mimi Cave's feature debut is still an over-the-top delight for anyone willing to roll with its surprisingly dark punches.
reviews.author: Valerie Ettenhofer

reviews.text: [Fresh] just never manages to live up to the considerable impact of its early scenes.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Fresh is a stylistic blast, even if it never lives up to its queasy potential or its electric performances.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Cave and Kahn have created something excitingly (pardon the pun) fresh, in the vein of horror comedies of the past few years, with a very different twist applied to it.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: Fresh is a super-fun survivor story filled with blood and guts and good music. Mimi Cave serves up one hell of a hilarious horror story with some sumptuous surprises.
reviews.author: Jonathan DeHaan

reviews.text: For those easily wooed by grossness and gore, Cave's black comedy has much to offer, though it relies heavily on a cliched third act rather than mining the cultural commentary driving the narrative.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Sebastian Stan gives off some serious American Psycho vibes in what might be his most engaging performance yet, an intoxicating cocktail of menace and charm that make him one of the most interesting cinematic psychopaths in recent memory.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: For Cave's first feature, Fresh is still wildly enjoyable. The concept is an exciting new vehicle for a spin on some well-worn tropes, giving them a facelift for today's audiences. If this is just the beginning, then the future looks bright.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: Fresh transitions from simmering romance to boiling carnage and in doing so becomes a deliciously moreish movie morsel.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: [Fresh] benefits immensely from the twisted chemistry of its leads, Cave's confidence behind the camera, and the spiky script devised by Lauryn Kahn.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: FRESH puts Mimi Cave on the map as a horror director.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: Just as Get Out offers a lacerating critique of white liberal racism, Fresh tears into toxic male sexuality and attitudes to women -- and there's obviously plenty of room for them both.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Fresh is sleek and nimble, a worthy new entry into the feminist revenge thriller genre.
reviews.author: Natalia Winkelman

reviews.text: As nauseating as it is, "Fresh" is very well-worn. If you've seen "Get Out" and "Promising Young Woman," which this is basically a mashup of, "Fresh" will leave you craving something meatier.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Fresh is pitched as a kind of genre corrective, except its tone-deaf cheekiness only results in a feeling of dreary regression.
reviews.author: Mark Hanson

reviews.text: Mimi Cave joins with screenwriter Lauryn Khan to deliver an energetic thriller that doesn't dig any deeper into its strong themes than it has to.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Cave has a smart, stylish way of storytelling that somehow makes a film built on bone saws and grotesqueries feel almost breezy.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Cave certainly has an eye for aesthetics, but Fresh attempts to find a middle ground between relationship satire and gross-out horror, becoming a bloody disappointment in the process.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Cave and her screenwriter, Lauryn Kahn, do almost all their savviest work at the start. But they have two leads who commit pretty perfectly.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: High octane feminist cinema in a Promising Young Woman meets Raw sort of way, this is a memorable, stomach-churning, socially conscious horror film that has something important to say.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The film lacks the necessary bite either in its body horror or humor to truly pull off its cannibalistic commentary.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Though the execution can be all over the place at times, Fresh shows all the signs of a new voice that's eager to tell something different on the big screen.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: A disturbingly gory feature that explores the horrifying side of modern dating, Fresh isn't for the faint of heart.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: FRESH is a satiating watch if you're looking to whet your horror palate.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: This is a horror movie that is pretty disgusting, not terribly clever, but one that Disney- yes, Disney- will release this year
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: Fresh is part romantic comedy, part thriller, and all fun. It is grotesque and disturbing at times, but also strangely satisfying. Sebastian Stan steals every scene he is in.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Darkly hilarious and genuinely disturbing... a nightmare rom-com that switches back and forth between the precision of a scalpel and the mayhem of a meat-tenderizer by ever-messier degrees as it goes
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: A true original
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Fresh is a demented delight, through and through. Skewering the modern dating scene while also telling a thriller tale we've never seen before, it weaves an enthralling web.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: An incredibly tense film, centred on Edgar-Jones and Stan's fantastic performances (the latter uses his charisma to terrify both Noa and the viewer). [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Sebastian Stan has never been better than he is here, with his mega-watt charisma turned up to eleven.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Stan is clearly having the time of his life with Cave's slick material, powering the narrative through its bloated runtime.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: This charming meet-cute whets your appetite with a delectable first course of allegory, style, and great characters. But it leaves you unsatiated when it comes to horror or the lively pitch-black humor it sporadically teases.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: "Fresh" is like "Hannibal" meets "Death Proof."
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The screenplay (which was written by Lauryn Kahn) successfully navigates genre changes, making "Fresh" a thrilling, exciting, and completely twisted ride to go on.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: If overly obvious as satire, surprisingly tame as horror, and a solid 20 minutes too long, Fresh is held aloft by committed performances from Daisy Edgar-Jones and Sebastian Stan.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: It's a symphony of tawdry elegance, a perfect, percolating mix of trash and class. Cave and Kahn have crafted a timeless, twisted AF feminist allegory.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: In the vein of Eli Roth's Hostel -- maybe Fresh is similarly an acquired taste.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Delivers on its titular promise with a toothsome array of horrors.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: Mimi Cave knows how to captivate and how to repulse, usually at the same time. Fresh is a breakneck emotional rollercoaster, and like many rollercoasters, it'll also make your stomach churn.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Hilarious, dark, on-the-nose about modern dating woes, and also a nightmare.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: Sebastian Stan eats up his best role yet, but the women of Fresh make this deliciously dark horror a must-see.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: With its darkly humorous writing, stellar acting, and incredible direction, 'Fresh' is a wild experience from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Cassondra Feltus

reviews.text: Sick but satisfying...
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: For those who like their dating movies with a bit of gristle, Fresh is a perfect match.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: Obscene, captivating - Fresh is a shocking horror movie that pushes all the wrong buttons in all the right ways.
reviews.author: Ty Cooper

reviews.text: Fresh may not exactly live up to its title as it caves (sorry Mimi) to familiar tropes of the horror genre in its second half, but in playing with the whole theme of consumption in all its meanings Kahn's outrageous script has points to make.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: It's totally insane, and I ate up every second of it. I almost want to bite my lip here not to reveal any more - just see it, and trust me on this.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: A film that lives up to its title. If Fresh stumbles on the way to its own finish line, it's still a hell of a way to launch a career.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: A meat-cute that gives new meaning to the phrase "eating butt."
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Thanks to a brilliant psychotic turn by Sebastian Stan and writer Lauryn Kahn's dry wit, Fresh feels like a horror film that is both urgent and entertaining.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: "FRESH" unthinkingly falls into all kinds of regressive and reactionary traps without leaving much space for discussion or disagreement.
reviews.author: Elena Lazic

reviews.text: Offers a lethal cocktail of social commentary and gruesome horror laced with the blackest of comedy.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Off-putting it may be, there's enough deliciousness throughout the wicked Fresh that your pallet is sure to be satisfied
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: FRESH is an impressive debut for Cave. Accompanied by Kahn's deliciously twisted screenplay and entertaining performances from Edgar-Jones and Stan, audiences will lap it up.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Channels many of the anxieties and fears of modern dating to create a film which you can get your teeth into.
reviews.author: Rob Aldam

reviews.text: Fresh is one of the most twisted, original horror film I've seen. My jaw was on the floor 30 minutes in and has remained so ever since. Sebastian Stan and Daisy Edgar-Jones are brilliant.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

synopsis: FRESH follows Noa (Daisy Edgar-Jones), who meets the alluring Steve (Sebastian Stan) at a grocery store and -- given her frustration with dating apps -- takes a chance and gives him her number. After their first date, Noa is smitten and accepts Steve's invitation to a romantic weekend getaway. Only to find that her new paramour has been hiding some unusual appetites.
